title: Hearty Smoked and Fermented Polish Salmon Pilaf
description: A fermented, snappy Polish dish featuring smoked salmon, perfect for a crowd-pleasing dinner.

ingredients.name: Smoked Salmon Fillets
ingredients.notes: Wild-caught and smoked in-house or store-bought

instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer until the water runs clear.
In a large clay pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the caraway seeds and cook for another minute, stirring constantly.
Add the smoked salmon fillets and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, until lightly browned.
Add the sauerkraut, rice, dill, salt, and black pepper to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and transfer it to a preheated tandoor or oven at 375°F (190°C).
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Remove the pot from the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Fluff the pilaf with a fork and serve hot.
Optional: Garnish with additional dill and serve with a dollop of sour cream, if desired.
